name: Observer azed crossword No 2,116
preamble: Clues are of two types. Acrosses are of Printer’s Devilry type. Each is a passage from which the printer has removed a hidden answer, closing the gap and sometimes taking liberties with the punctuation, but not disturbing the order of the remaining letters. Example: Vaulting above tunnel entrance appears inane, scary. Answer: PESTO. Undevilled version: Vaulting above tunnel entrance appears in an escape story. Every passage, when complete, makes sense. Each down clue, except one, has been distorted by the superfluous addition at any point (i.e. beginning or ending at a word break or within a word in the clue) of a consecutive jumble of the letters of one of the across answers. Solvers will need to remove the intrusive jumbles before they can solve the clues, which make a modicum of sense when the jumbles are removed. Closing up the gap may require some manipulation of the clue’s punctuation, but there is no further tinkering with word-division elsewhere in the clue. Jumbled across answers have been inserted in down clues in clue order, i.e. 1 Across in 1 Down, 7 Across in 2 Down, …, 34 Across in 29 Down. Competitors should submit with their entries a clue to 15 Down, which may be defined as part of the puzzle’s title but is otherwise unclued, in the style of the other down clues, with the jumble of the appropriate across answer included. Please underline the superfluous jumble in your clue. NB Preference will be given to clues which make sense in both their original and their expanded forms. Every answer is in The Chambers Dictionary (2011), including one abbreviation.
